_comment: Hand-curated 'What's new' per OpenClaw minor + channel, shown on the Upgrade page. Admin language only (no internal jargon — see the plan's D1 table). tests/server/openclaw-whats-new.test.js fails when the pinned beta minor has no entry, so bumping the tested beta means updating this file. lastVerifiedVersion is the newest release this entry was verified against; the UI notes when the channel has moved past it.

highlights.title: Node 24.16 or newer required
highlights.body: The 2026.9 line no longer runs on Node 22 or 25 — it needs Node 24.16+ (or 26.1+) because older runtimes can truncate SQLite text. AlphaClaw v0.9.80 moved its image to Node 24.16+; if this AlphaClaw's own Node is older than a release requires, the catalog row says so and the update is refused before anything downloads.

highlights.title: Agent database moves to schema 21
highlights.body: 2026.9.5 upgrades every agent database to schema 21 and 2026.9.4 moved the state database to schema 17; older builds cannot open either. AlphaClaw takes and verifies a backup before applying, and going back means restoring that backup with the matching older build — reinstalling the older package alone is not enough.

highlights.title: Updates rehearse before switching
highlights.body: Atomic Updates check the next version against a private copy of your setup while the current gateway keeps running, then switch over and verify. Recovery can restore the previous version when your data is still compatible, and updates that fail now report the root cause first and restore the service they stopped.

highlights.title: Add plugins without a restart
highlights.body: Supported plugins can be installed, reloaded, enabled or disabled while the gateway stays up, and a running update also checks eligible plugins even when the core is already current.

highlights.title: Backups capture more, more safely
highlights.body: Full backups now include the extra settings files your main config refers to, preserve linked and hardlinked databases and Mac metadata files, and can verify the archive as it is written. Archives from 2026.9.5 may not restore on 2026.9.4 or older.

highlights.title: Legacy repairs wait for Doctor
highlights.body: Older conversations, workspace metadata, pairing records and file-based message queues are no longer converted during ordinary startup. When OpenClaw reports pending legacy repairs, AlphaClaw's Doctor run (openclaw doctor --fix, gateway stopped) completes them; restarting alone does not.

highlights.title: Archive and share conversations
highlights.body: Inactive history can be compressed into cold storage and reopened later (off by default; 30 days when on), and selected conversation groups can be shared read-only with a paired OpenClaw installation.

highlights.title: Replies survive restarts
highlights.body: Active, queued and delegated replies are recovered after a gateway restart instead of being dropped, interrupted memory rebuilds reuse completed work, and healthy agents stay online while another agent's database is checked.

securityFlips.warning: Session tools can list, search and address sessions belonging to OTHER agents on this gateway by default. Set it to "tree", "agent" or "self" after upgrading to keep each agent's sessions to itself.
Ordinary agent-to-agent access is on by default, so one agent can send to and read another's sessions. Set enabled to false, or list the allowed agent pairs in allow, to restrict it.
Agents can spawn concurrent sub-agents (Swarm) by default, which multiplies the work — and the token spend — one request can trigger. Set it to false after upgrading to keep sub-agents opt-in.

Since 2026.9.3 the new-session model picker shows supported CLI agents and can create native CLI sessions without a separate opt-in. Set it to false after upgrading if this box should not launch CLI agents.

Since 2026.9.5 agents with the message tool can send to and act across EVERY configured chat service without a separate opt-in — and this also changes existing installs that left the key unset. Set it to false after upgrading (and allowWithinProvider to false to confine replies to the originating conversation) to restore the old isolation.

highlights.title: Team access
highlights.body: Multiple people can use one agent with their own identity: profiles and avatars, a who's-online roster, messages attributed to their author, and per-member permissions.

highlights.title: Shared secret store
highlights.body: A team-wide place for API keys and tokens, managed from the OpenClaw dashboard (Settings → Secrets). Secrets can be locked to exact destination hosts.

highlights.title: Verified database backups
highlights.body: Compact, verified snapshots of OpenClaw's databases with safe restore to a fresh location.

highlights.title: GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna
highlights.body: OpenAI's newest models work across both the OpenClaw and Codex engines, with model, engine, and thinking level switching together.

highlights.title: New channels
highlights.body: ClickClack gains a paste-one-code guided setup; Buzz connects agents to team rooms.

highlights.title: Better managed restarts
highlights.body: OpenClaw now understands that AlphaClaw manages its lifecycle, so restarts and updates coordinate instead of colliding.

securityFlips.warning: The OpenClaw dashboard gains a host terminal by default. Anyone with admin access to the dashboard can run commands on this server. Turn it off after upgrading if you don't want that.
Agent-initiated skill changes now apply without asking. Set the policy to "pending" after upgrading to keep an approval step.
Slack progress switches from emoji reaction updates to Slack's native thread status. Re-enable status reactions in the Slack channel settings if your team relies on them.
